content: 1. It is now recommended to monitor serum creatinine and potassium levels 7 to 14 days after initiating treatment with ACE inhibitors, ARBs, or diuretics. 2. Bempedoic acid therapy has been included as an option for individuals with diabetes who are intolerant to statins and do not have established cardiovascular disease. 3. A new subsection addressing statin therapy intolerance has been added, which recommends alternative cholesterol-lowering therapies such as PCSK9 inhibitors. 4. It is advised to involve a cardiovascular or neurological specialist to determine the appropriate duration of dual antiplatelet therapy for individuals with diabetes following an acute coronary syndrome or stroke. 5. Screening for asymptomatic heart failure by measuring natriuretic peptides has been added to help prevent progression to symptomatic heart failure. 6. Screening for peripheral artery disease using the ankle-brachial index (ABI) is now recommended for asymptomatic individuals with diabetes, particularly those with microvascular disease or a diabetes duration of more than 10 years. 7. The use of SGLT1/2 inhibitors is recommended for individuals with diabetes and heart failure to reduce the risks of heart failure and cardiovascular-related death.
